summary: The history test was read and frozen: every pre-registered stock rule was rejected against random baskets from this same list, and simply holding every name equally did better than any rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. Today's four calls are all neutral and low, unchanged from recent runs, and nothing here is expected to beat the index. All of it is pretend money; the household's real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain tested its stock-picking rules on old races, and stocks picked out of a hat did as well or better. So today it only looks at four stocks with pretend money, like a kid looking at toys in a shop window. The real money stays in one big basket that holds a bit of every company.

Pershing Square's disclosed book holds it bullish; the fund's matured record is too thin to prove anything, and this call neither follows nor fights it. Unchanged from the last runs.
